notes.title: First Official SAS Merch Available for Purchase Now!
notes.content:
Today we are thrilled to announce that we are launching our brand new online store with the first-ever collection of official SAS merch, hand-crafted by our talented artists!

This initial collection includes a variety of unisex shirts, available in both short sleeve and long sleeve, featuring designs that have been carefully arranged to incorporate elements from SAS. From the game’s logo, which uses both English and Japanese characters, to the butterfly design that captures Chouko’s tragic backstory, to the landmarks that represent the game’s road-tripping premise and blend of Japanese and American culture, each piece of apparel reflects an aspect of the game’s unique world, story, and sensibilities.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41754942/a16f4005ad488b531b53ea8d93f1a7fa1d36b587.png[/img]

For the time being, orders will only be processed within the United States and Canada, although we intend to further expand access to our offerings over time. As an independent studio, all profits from the store will greatly help us to complete the remaining development on SAS and we are grateful to everyone who chooses to support us by purchasing a shirt and showing off their excitement for the game!

To check out the new store and the full collection of apparel, head on over to:
[h3][b][url=merch.showaamericanstory.com]merch.showaamericanstory.com[/url][/b][/h3]

notes.title: 【The last working day of 2023! Happy New Year to everyone in advance!】
Showa American Story is like a horny Dead Rising set in apocalyptic Japanese America
notes.content:
Showa American Story is an action-RPG set in Japan-controlled 1980s America after a zombie apocalypse in which you shoot zombies while upgrading your character and the RV she lives in. I don't know if it's going to be good, but the trailer makes a heck of an impression, calling forth the spirit of sorts of lovably janky PlayStation 2 and Wii era action games.

The trailer really does have it all, from B-movie hyperviolence to the weighty, slapstick combat of zombie games like Dead Rising. There are Nier Automata-like bullet hell segments and No More Heroes-like "living activities" minigames. There are bicycling zombies and satellites crashing into the planet. It's got a catchy Asian pop song and long, lingering shots of the main character's butt, which I guess is at least in keeping with the B-movie aesthetics.

Showa American Story comes to us from Nekcom Entertainment, a Chinese studio which had previously worked on a horror series simply called Dying. (Dying: Reborn - I promise I'm not making that title up - is on Steam.) There's no announced release date for the upcoming zombie game yet, but it does have a Steam page, and is set to release across PC, PlayStation 4, and PlayStation 5.
